evidence.finding: Mean service level fell from 89.34% before the incident to 50.32% from 09:15 onward, a decline of 39.02 percentage points.
Mean ASA rose from 27.69 seconds to 77.29 seconds after the incident boundary, consistent with material queueing pressure.
Mean AHT increased from 373.89 to 517.87 seconds after 09:15, a 38.51% increase.
Mean offered calls increased from 72.4 to 85.64 per interval, an 18.28% increase; this was material pressure but smaller than the AHT increase.

primary_root_cause_detail: A sustained increase in average handle time after 09:15 reduced processing throughput and drove the service-level decline; demand rose moderately and may have added pressure.
recommended_actions: Investigate the post-09:15 drivers of longer handle time by queue, contact reason, hold time, and after-call work.
Restore AHT to baseline through targeted operational support while protecting quality and resolution outcomes.
Maintain short-term overflow or reserve capacity until AHT and queue wait metrics normalize.
stakeholder_summary: The service-level incident was most likely driven by a sustained 38.5% increase in handle time after 09:15, which reduced throughput and increased waits. Offered demand also rose 18.3% and contributed pressure, but the available center-level evidence indicates handle time was the primary cause.
